question: A physician attempts to study cirrhosis in his state. Using a registry of admitted patients over the last 10 years at the local hospital, he isolates all patients who have been diagnosed with cirrhosis. Subsequently, he contacts this group of patients, asking them to complete a survey assessing their prior exposure to alcohol use, intravenous drug abuse, blood transfusions, personal history of cancer, and other medical comorbidities. An identical survey is given to an equal number of patients in the registry who do not carry a prior diagnosis of cirrhosis. Which of the following is the study design utilized by this physician?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Exposure assessment -> Comparison of groups with and without cirrhosis -> Case-control study design -> 95% confidence. CHAIN: Survey completion on cirrhosis patients and non-cirrhosis patients -> Data collection on alcohol use, drug abuse, transfusions, cancer history -> Case-control study design -> 95%
enhanced_information: The study design utilized by the physician in this scenario is a case-control study. This is supported by the chain of exposure assessment, comparison of groups with and without cirrhosis, and data collection on alcohol use, drug abuse, transfusions, and cancer history. The evidence path mentioning blood transfusions is not directly relevant to the study design but provides insight into potential factors associated with liver cirrhosis.
analysis: The study design utilized by the physician in this scenario involves selecting patients with cirrhosis (cases) and patients without cirrhosis (controls) and then assessing their prior exposures and characteristics. This aligns with the definition of a case-control study where the researcher starts with the outcome (cirrhosis) and looks back to investigate potential causes or associations. The evidence provided supports this conclusion by describing the comparison of groups based on cirrhosis status and exposure assessment.
